summary: A Glacier National Park lookout above the Nyack valley with conflicting build dates (1929-1933) across sources; still standing.

facts.design: Two-story wooden cab, 14x14-ft, similar to Apgar but with angle-braced catwalk

access.note: Reachable by trail from Nyack Ranger Station; no source confirms public entry is permitted

visit.trail_note: Reached by trail from Nyack Ranger Station

events.note: firelookout.com describes an earlier 1928 cabin destroyed by fire; not corroborated elsewhere
firelookout.com dates the present cab to 1929
NHLR description and Wikipedia infobox both give 1930 for the present structure
Wikipedia's article text separately states the structure was built in 1933, contradicting its own infobox

evidence.quote: Loneman Lookout is a 14'x14' lookout similar to Apgar except the catwalk is shored with angle supports. Built in 1930, it is reached by trail from Nyack Ranger Station.
The low two-story timber-construction structure with a pyramidal roof was built in 1933.
Built in 1930, it is one several similar structures built in a program to establish an overlapping chain of fire lookouts in the park.

evidence.supports: 1929 build replacing 1928 cabin destroyed by fire, and 1998 renovation
evidence.quote: This 2-story NPS frame cab, built in 1929, replaced a 1928 cabin that was destroyed in a forest fire. It was completely renovated in 1998

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Three different build years appear across sources (1929, 1930, 1933), and Wikipedia's own infobox (1930) contradicts its article text (1933). The story reports all three rather than picking one.

notes_for_editor: Build date is genuinely unsettled across sources, including within Wikipedia's own article. No staffing history or fire history found beyond the disputed earlier-cabin-fire claim from firelookout.com.
